newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU tells UK BA-American cannot sell slots. [CORRECTED 17:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: EU tells UK BA-American cannot sell slots. [CORRECTED 17:35 GMT]

text.p: The European Commission was to tell the British authorities later on Friday that under EU legislation British Airways and American Airlines could not sell airport slots to gain approval for their alliance, a Commission spokesman said.

"We were asked by the (British) Department of Trade and Industry to comment on the interpretation of the (EU's) civil aviation regulation in connection with the BA-AA merger," he told Reuters adding: "The answer to be given today is that slot-selling is illegal and this applies to the merger."
(Corrects to Department of Trade and Industry from Department of Transport, following an official correction by Commission)
He said this reflected the view of both European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert as well as his transport counterpart Neil Kinnock.
Although Van Miert's opinion was well known, airline analysts had expected Kinnock to take a more flexible approach on the issue.

The Commission's reaction comes after Britain's Office of Fair Trading proposed in December to clear the transatlantic alliance on the condition that the companies release a total of 168 weekly takeoff and landing slots at London's Heathrow airport to allow in new competition.
BA has agreed to it on the condition that it received financial compensation.

But a European Union regulation of 1993 only provides for the exchange, not the trading, of slots. Unused rights are supposed to be made available freely to existing competitors or new market entrants, according to the same rules.

Kinnock is said to favour a revision of the regulation which would authorise a secondary market for slots under certain conditions, but EU sources said that he will face a stiff opposition from Van Miert.

The Commission's reaction closes a week of fierce lobbying by rival U.S. airlines also opposed to the alliance due to fears it will limit competition between the U.S. and Britain and continental Europe.
BA and American submitted their agreement for clearance to the U.S. Department of Transportation earlier on Friday.
